summary: A 100-foot Aermotor fire tower near Gordon, Wisconsin, built in 1935, decommissioned by the state in 2015 and saved by local volunteers, with scheduled free climbs and a cabin rental listed in 2021-2022 reports.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor steel tower, likely an MC-39 model, with a Forest Service-style stairway whose treads and landings were upgraded to expanded steel

access.note: Free public climbs on scheduled days, run by the nonprofit owner. A one-room cabin at the base is rented through Airbnb.

visit.trail_note: Free climbs on scheduled Sundays (every other Sunday from May through October in one undated report); the Friends group publishes its dates

facts.agency: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources (operated the tower until 2015); the site is now owned by the Friends of the Bird Sanctuary

events.note: Register dates the tower to August 1935 at a site about 736 ft elevation; it was later moved to its current location at an unknown date
Staffed intermittently during spring fire season until 2015
Decommissioned by the Wisconsin DNR and set to be torn down
Cabin moved to the site, listed as of September 2020; the 2021 news report says it was donated and moved from a nearby lake
Tower and one-room cabin opened for rentals through Airbnb, nightly fee from $67

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says Douglas County has been working with a Friends of the Bird Sanctuary group to preserve the tower; a 2021 news report says the nonprofit now owns the site. The story reports the 2021 ownership and the register's account of the county's role is not repeated.

A Central US Lookouts entry dated September 2020 says a cabin had been moved to the site; a 2021 news report says the cabin was donated and moved from a nearby lake. The two are not contradictory, and the story gives both without choosing a date for the move.

notes_for_editor: The register is the only source for the first site (about 736 ft) and the later move; no other source I read mentions a move, so that claim is single-sourced. The record's agency is the former operator (WI DNR); the current owner is the Friends of the Bird Sanctuary per the 2021 news report, and the record's ownership 'unknown' could be updated, but no correction is proposed because the record does not claim an owner. The 2015 decommissioning and 2017 NHLR registration match the record. Staffing and climb schedule details come from 2021-2022 reports and may have changed; the 2026 status of the open-climb schedule was not checked. The Airbnb listing was not read directly (JavaScript-heavy), so the rental is supported only by the 2021 article and the FFLA rentals list. Four web reads, one WebSearch (the second was not needed).
